page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.6xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 24 dedicated physical cores and 24 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with single-thread-per-core execution. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and a massive 15,000 GB local NVMe SSD storage array. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 38 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory and database capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in Passmark database operations and Passmark memory scores, alongside top-tier large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 378.34 GB/sec. Multi-threaded performance is strong, as demonstrated by Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, and multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression. However, single-core CPU tasks, ray tracing, and image processing fall within the average range. Large-model LLM inference speeds are poor, indicating a tradeoff where the instance is less suited for heavy AI generation tasks compared to its storage and memory strengths.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i8ge.6xlarge offers high resource density by combining an efficient ARM64 architecture with substantial local NVMe storage and memory capacity. This makes it a highly viable option for workloads requiring high-speed local data access without the overhead of external storage. The instance is optimally suited for high-throughput database operations, large-scale data caching, static web serving, software compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive data processing workloads.
